claim: “Means and instrument adjuncts are characteristically realised by PPs headed by by (or by means) and with (or without) respectively”, with [12iia] She opened my door with the master-key. On p. 665, [1ii] They opened it with a tin-opener is labelled “[instrument: §2.2]”.
evidence_summary: Ch. 4, §8.3.4 (p. 319), gives [76ia] We opened the door with the master-key as a construction with “object + non-core complement within the VP”, and p. 320 says: “The non-core complements in the [a] examples of [76] have a range of roles. With the master-key in [ia] is an instrument.” Chapter 8 sends the reader to that passage (p. 674, CG-0121).
finding: Medium confidence. The same verb, object and PP are an adjunct in Ch. 8 and a complement in Ch. 4, and Ch. 8 doesn’t flag instrumental complements as §2.1 flags manner complements. Ch. 4 may count the PP as a complement because it alternates with the subject in [76ib], and Ch. 4, p. 219, admits “some uncertainty, and disagreement among grammarians, as to how much should be subsumed under the function complement”. That explains the analysis but not the silence between the chapters.
inference: Is instrumental with the master-key an adjunct?

evidence.passage: §2.2, p. 673. “Means and instrument adjuncts are characteristically realised by PPs”.
evidence.example: Ch. 4, p. 320, on [76ia] We opened the door with the master-key.
evidence.establishes: Two chapters assign the instrumental PP different functions without comment.
